BLS Assessor Course

  • Peer-to-peer BLS/AED assessment using standardised assessment tool
  • Assessment verdict delivery and communication skills
  • Assessment of the borderline candidate
  • Group consensus regarding grey areas

BLS Provider Recertification

Assessor Course

Assessment night

  • Preparing your room
  • Environment
  • Equipment
  • Checklist
  • Role of teachers
  • When to have assistant in or out of the room
  • Timing
  • Clean up
Encouragement of checklist use and empowering assessors to request replacement equipment if any concerns e.g. non-sticky pads, low AED batteries. Debate on whether to have the assistant step out for verdict (previous consensus that does not need to be routine practice)

Assessment night

Assessment of the successful candidate

  • Introduction
  • Making the candidate feel at ease
  • Reassurance about assessor use of phone
  • Delivering the verdict
  • Learning conversation
  • Closure
Discussions around the opening gambit, explanation of phone/tablet/laptop use (and the context about mistaken QCPR), discussion around verdict delivery and avoiding delaying verdict or giving too much feedback.

Assessment of the successful candidate

  • Group sessions

Assessment of the unsuccessful candidate

  • Delivering the verdict
  • Be direct
  • Learning conversation
  • Re-sits
  • Avoid confrontation/debate
Discussion/debate on how to deliver an unsuccessful verdict, discussion about focusing on the most salient fail points (and the context of complaints where a candidate has latched on to a minor issue mentioned first), discussion about what to do with the candidate once the fail verdict is given, discussion about having the assistant step outside for the verdict or not.

Assessment of the unsuccessful candidate

  • Group sessions

Standardisation

  • No help at beginning of scenario
  • Candidates will practise with and without help in classes
  • Expect candidate to Call - Check - CPR
  • Allow candidate to complete (at least) one full uninterrupted set of 30 compressions prior to shock
  • Can do this before or after assistant offers help (and candidate asks them for AED)
  • Can do further full sets after shock if need to judge further

Issues from previous assessments

  • Poor head tilt chin lift + inadequate rescue breaths
  • No pinch of nose during breaths
  • Candidate pausing CPR when assistant offers them help
  • Not checking for response/breathing before or after recovery position
  • A few candidates are unaware they are expected to do the full run-through
  • Candidate thinking they were being assessed with QCPR (not aware of phone use reason)
  • Staring at assessor during shock

Course closure

  • Form completion
  • First night debrief
  • Assessment irregularity Google form
  • Assessment sit-ins

SUMMARY

  • Prepare for assessment night and use checklist
  • Re-familiarise with grey areas before assessment night
  • Avoid having document open during assessments (or WhatsApp messages mid-assessment)
  • Standardised approach
  • Feel empowered to fail borderline/poor performance
  • Student/Senior Faculty will support your decision making
  • Document fail reasons well on assessment form
  • Raise recurrent issues. Repeated issues are fed back to instructors
  • This feedback has been instrumental in improving candidate performance
